anodal_tdcs.name: Anodal tDCS (Left Temporoparietal)
anodal_tdcs.short_description: Anodal tDCS to left temporoparietal cortex applied during concurrent behavioural therapy to boost cortical excitability and augment LTP- like plasticity; efficacy moderated by BDNF Val66Met genotype.

auditory_temporal_processing.units: FM detection threshold (modulation index); lower values = better performance (inverse scale)

bdnf_val66met.units: genotype category: val/val (typical) vs Met-allele carrier (atypical)

communicative_shaping.name: Communicative Shaping
communicative_shaping.short_description: Graded increase in verbal demand within structured communicative tasks, reinforcing successive approximations toward more complex propositional speech.

inhibitory_rtms.name: Inhibitory rTMS (Right Pars Triangularis / BA45)
inhibitory_rtms.short_description: Slow (1 Hz) inhibitory rTMS to right pars triangularis to suppress maladaptive right IFG overactivity, reducing transcallosal inhibition of left perilesional language cortex and improving naming fluency.

listen_repeat_cycle.name: Listen–Repeat–Spell–Copy–Spell Cycle
listen_repeat_cycle.short_description: Five-step training cycle (listen → repeat → spell → copy → re-spell) that combines phonological activation with errorless encoding and retrieval practice to strengthen phonological-to-orthographic conversion.

massed_practice.name: Massed Practice
massed_practice.short_description: High-frequency, concentrated repetition of target behaviours across sessions. A dose parameter shared across CIAT, MIT, and Spell-Study- Spell that drives activity-dependent plasticity in perilesional cortex.

melodic_intoning.name: Melodic Intoning
melodic_intoning.short_description: Singing target utterances on two pitches with exaggerated prosody and progressive fading of clinician support; the core procedure of MIT that recruits right-hemisphere speech-motor pathways.

phonological_feature_analysis.name: Phonological Feature Analysis
phonological_feature_analysis.short_description: Systematic picture-cued analysis of a target word's first phoneme, final phoneme, syllable count, rhyme, and phoneme-sharing word to strengthen lexical-phonological retrieval via spreading activation.

retrieval_practice.name: Retrieval Practice
retrieval_practice.short_description: Active recall attempts before feedback, exploiting the testing effect to strengthen long-term retention of trained word forms beyond what restudy alone achieves.

rhythmic_hand_tapping.name: Rhythmic Left-Hand Tapping
rhythmic_hand_tapping.short_description: Left-hand rhythmic tapping on each syllable, co-occurring with melodic intoning to engage right somatomotor cortex and provide temporal cueing for articulatory onset.

semantic_feature_generation.name: Semantic Feature Generation
semantic_feature_generation.short_description: Guided generation of semantic features (category, function, properties, location, association) for a pictured target, driving spreading activation through the semantic network to support lexical retrieval.

severity_metric.name: Aphasia severity metric (instrument-agnostic)
severity_metric.units: varies by instrument — see `instrument` field on each finding

stroke_severity_sss.name: Neurological stroke severity (Scandinavian Stroke Scale)
stroke_severity_sss.units: score 0–58 (SSS) or 0–42 (modified SSS); higher score = less severe impairment

typicality_ordering.name: Typicality-Based Training Order
typicality_ordering.short_description: Sequencing training items from most to least typical within a semantic category to exploit prototype effects and stabilise semantic attractors before training peripheral category members.

verb_argument_structure_training.name: Verb Argument Structure Training
verb_argument_structure_training.short_description: Meta-linguistic training of verb argument structure and thematic- syntactic mapping using complex (non-canonical) sentence structures; drives generalisation to simpler structures via CATE and recruits right-hemisphere syntactic networks.

verbal_constraint.name: Verbal Constraint
verbal_constraint.short_description: Complete prohibition of gesture and non-verbal compensatory strategies, forcing the patient to use verbal communication exclusively during CIAT sessions.

left_extreme_capsule.basis: Same structure; reachable only through the disconnectome.

extreme_capsule.basis: ENIGMA has an extreme-capsule bundle; no label atlas used by the report does, so this unit exists only for the disconnectome (EVIDENCE_GAPS.md, "extreme capsule ventral stream").
extreme_capsule.name: Extreme capsule

arcuate_fasciculus.basis: ENIGMA arcuate fasciculus (whole bundle; its segments are not separated).

forceps.basis: Midline bundles without a side, like JHU's forceps labels; the side is taken from the lesion voxels. ENIGMA also has callosal body bundles, which JHU does not label, so they are not used here to keep the unit's meaning the same in both reports.

frontal_aslant_tract.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

ifof.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

ilf.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

middle_longitudinal_fasciculus.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

optic_radiation.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

slf.basis: ENIGMA separates SLF II and SLF III (its SLF I sits under the cingulum). Together they are the fronto-parietal body of the SLF that JHU's single label covers.

slf_iii.basis: ENIGMA SLF III, the same bundle XTRACT labels.

uncinate_fasciculus.basis: ENIGMA bundle of the same tract.

bilateral_middle_frontal_gyrus_recovery.basis: The entry concerns the middle frontal gyrus of both hemispheres. Its aliases also list right temporo-occipital MTG and right supramarginal gyrus, which are not mapped here.

corpus_callosum.basis: Only the callosal forceps are labelled in JHU (units.yaml, forceps).

ho-cort_44.basis: Legacy entry for HarvardOxford cortical label 44 region (IFG pars opercularis, BA 44); the entry is the left one.

left_anterior_arcuate_fasciculus.basis: The anterior segment (Catani et al. 2005) links the inferior frontal and inferior parietal cortex: in XTRACT, SLF III.

left_anterior_temporal_lobe.basis: Anterior temporal lobe as the entry defines it (aliases ATL, temporal pole) = temporal pole with the anterior superior and middle temporal gyri.

left_anterior_temporal_lobe__Robson2014.basis: Robson et al. 2014 region; its aliases add the anterior fusiform gyrus to the anterior temporal lobe.

left_arcuate_fasciculus_slf.basis: The entry combines the arcuate and the SLF ("dorsal language pathway"), so XTRACT's arcuate and JHU's SLF.

left_dorsolateral_prefrontal_cortex.basis: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (BA 9/46) lies mainly on the middle frontal gyrus; the atlases have no DLPFC label.

left_dorsomedial_prefrontal_cortex.basis: The dorsomedial prefrontal cortex is the medial superior frontal gyrus (AAL Frontal_Sup_Medial).

left_inferior_frontal_occipital_fascicul.basis: Spelling variant of the inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus.

left_insular_precentral_gyrus_cluster.basis: Alias of left_precentral_gyrus_insula in Dronkers1996 (R001, R002); the source describes the same discrete region. Inherits the whole-insula approximation; does not localise the source cluster precisely.

left_long_segment_arcuate_fasciculus.basis: The long (direct fronto-temporal) segment is part of XTRACT's arcuate, which does not separate the segments.

left_occipito_temporal_sulcus.basis: The occipito-temporal sulcus has no atlas label; it separates the inferior temporal and fusiform gyri, whose temporo-occipital parts are used.

left_parietal_association_cortex.basis: Parietal association cortex = inferior parietal lobule (supramarginal, angular) and superior parietal lobule.

left_posterior_arcuate_fasciculus.basis: The posterior (temporo-parietal) segment has no XTRACT label; XTRACT's arcuate is the closest tract.

left_posterior_middle_temporal_gyrus.basis: Same structure (the temporo-occipital part is not included).

left_posterior_planum_temporale_spt.basis: Area Spt lies in the posterior planum temporale, which the atlases do not subdivide.

left_precentral_gyrus_insula.basis: The "precentral gyrus of the insula" (Dronkers 1996, apraxia of speech) is the superior precentral gyrus OF THE INSULA, not the motor precentral gyrus; the atlases do not subdivide the insula, so the whole insula is used.

left_precentral_gyrus_of_the_insula.basis: Alias of left_precentral_gyrus_insula in Dronkers1996 (R003); the same discrete insular region. Inherits the existing whole-insula approximation, not an exact cluster mask.

left_premotor_cortex.basis: Premotor cortex (BA 6) has no atlas label; it spans the anterior precentral gyrus laterally and the supplementary motor area medially.

left_rolandic_operculum.basis: The Rolandic operculum is HarvardOxford's central opercular cortex.

left_slf.basis: Han2016 explicitly expands left SLF as left superior longitudinal fasciculus. Same anatomical tract as left_superior_longitudinal_fasciculus. The study used JHU at 25 percent probability; the reporting unit uses a 50 percent core, so this is an anatomical link, not an identical study mask or FA measurement.

left_spgi.basis: Baldo2011 names the left superior precentral gyrus of the insula (SPGI). Same anatomical referent as left_precentral_gyrus_insula; inherits the whole-insula approximation, not a representation of the study's significant voxels.

left_superior_temporal_gyrus.basis: Whole superior temporal gyrus (aliases name both anterior and posterior parts).

left_superior_temporal_gyrus__Leff2009.basis: Leff et al. 2009 region (aliases posterior STG, posterior superior temporal sulcus, planum temporale); the sulcus has no atlas label.

left_superior_temporal_gyrus_wernicke.basis: Wernicke's area as the entry defines it (aliases: posterior STG, planum temporale).

left_superior_temporal_sulcus.basis: The superior temporal sulcus has no atlas label; it lies between the superior and middle temporal gyri, whose posterior divisions are used.

left_supramarginal_gyrus_premotor.basis: The entry groups the supramarginal gyrus with the inferior postcentral gyrus (aliases).

left_temporal_lobe.basis: All lateral and basal temporal units.

left_temporal_pole_mtg.basis: Middle temporal part of the temporal pole (AAL Temporal_Pole_Mid).

left_temporal_pole_stg.basis: Superior temporal part of the temporal pole (AAL Temporal_Pole_Sup).

left_temporobasal__Goldenberg1994.basis: Basal temporal cortex (Goldenberg 1994) = inferior temporal and fusiform gyri.

left_temporoparietal_junction.basis: The temporoparietal junction has no atlas label; taken as the posterior superior temporal, posterior supramarginal and angular gyri.

right_lateral_frontal_cortex.basis: Lateral frontal cortex taken as the inferior and middle frontal gyri.

right_medial_frontal_cortex.basis: Medial frontal cortex = HarvardOxford frontal medial cortex plus the medial superior frontal gyrus.

right_middle_temporal_gyrus.basis: Whole middle temporal gyrus, right hemisphere.

right_posterior_perisylvian_cortex.basis: Posterior perisylvian cortex taken as the posterior superior temporal gyrus, planum temporale and supramarginal gyrus.

coverage.need: The inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus has 3 findings; the anterior thalamic radiation (measured by JHU) none. Both were linked to semantic deficits and verbal fluency in stroke cohorts that measured tract damage directly.
3 findings on the inferior temporal gyrus and 5 on the fusiform gyrus, regions often damaged by posterior cerebral artery strokes and relevant to naming and reading.

7 findings, but neither JHU nor XTRACT labels the extreme capsule. Oeckel et al. 2021 and Kümmerer et al. 2013 measured it with tractography-derived templates from healthy subjects; extracting them documents the ventral-stream evidence, and their templates (if shared) would make the region reachable.

3 findings on the supplementary motor area and 1 on the frontal aslant tract (reachable since the XTRACT atlas was added), which connects it to the inferior frontal gyrus and is linked to verbal fluency after stroke.

The insula's role in apraxia of speech rests mainly on Dronkers 1996 (precentral gyrus of the insula) and is disputed: Hillis et al. 2004 placed it in the posterior inferior frontal gyrus instead. The frontal operculum has no finding at all. Both sides should be in the KB.
Every right-hemisphere region has 1-3 findings. Right-hemisphere structure and its role in recovery matter for interpreting a left-hemisphere lesion (and for right-hemisphere or bilateral lesions).

Lesions often reach the thalamus, caudate, putamen and pallidum (AAL measures all four), but the KB has no finding on the thalamus or caudate and 4 findings from one paper on putamen and pallidum (Radanovic & Mansur 2017 was extracted as a narrative review, without region-level findings). The subcortical-aphasia literature also shows that much of it reflects cortical hypoperfusion, which the report should be able to say.
